findings.text: s1(1) admits the MAST-U stored-coefficients arm at "unqualified near 4.9e-10" with no tolerance, while the other three arms of the same sentence are admitted at "within a factor of three" of a stated value; the arm's only discriminating fact is that the residual exceeds 1e-10 (the cited receipt is `4.864113698736961e-10`, converged=true, qualified=false, `docs/evidence/fragments/inverse-equilibrium-baseline/efit-comparison.html:1593`), so "near" admits any value a worker declines to call far

findings.reason: an undefined unit for the one cross-check between batched and solo states makes that clause either vacuous or impossible, and a worker must be told which quantity is meant.
findings.text: s4(2) requires each batched state to agree with the same state solved alone "to within ten times the threshold in flux", but the threshold is a relative terminal residual (1e-10) and the clause names no norm for the flux difference: absolute Wb, a fraction of the ~70 Wb axis-to-boundary span, and a relative residual are three numbers differing by orders of magnitude at this scale, so one reading is trivially met and another is out of reach

findings.reason: the two readings imply different repairs, and done-when clause (1) is unscorable until the one meant is fixed, since the flag must be both per-state and returned.
findings.text: the endpoint "returns a per-state converged flag and residual without leaving the device" contradicts itself and its own evidence: the base-revision refusal the receipts record is a host conversion taken inside the traced solve (`bool(np.asarray(history.converged))`, reached only for `newton_krylov`, `nova/equilibrium/forward.py:1971-1972`), whereas a flag reported in the record must reach the host after the solve returns, so "without leaving the device" cannot be read literally and the plan does not say whether the repaired solve may return host-resident per-state arrays or must keep each flag device-resident
